title: Testing ROS 2 Nodes
text:
Automated testing catches regressions before they reach the UAV. This page covers unit tests for isolated logic and integration tests that launch real nodes against a mock DDS bridge or a full PX4 SITL.
The integration test patterns follow the official ROS 2 integration testing tutorial, adapted for PX4 nodes and a colcon + pixi workspace.

title: Testing ROS 2 Nodes
Testing ROS 2 Nodes
text:
Integration tests
Integration tests launch actual nodes and verify behaviour over real topics. The key tool is the launch_testing package, which wraps a ROS 2 launch file with a unittest harness.






Important



Integration tests rely on unittest, not pytest. Do not mix them in the same file — post-shutdown tests silently disappear when the file is wrapped by pytest.



Test file structure
Integration test files live in test/test_*.py. Four elements make up every launch test:







Element
Purpose




generate_test_description()
Declares what to launch, analogous to generate_launch_description


launch_testing.actions.ReadyToTest()
Signals the framework that nodes are ready and active tests can start


Undecorated unittest.TestCase subclass
Active tests that run while nodes are alive


@launch_testing.post_shutdown_test() subclass
Tests that run after all nodes exit (e.g. exit-code checks)





Example: controller node test
import time
import unittest

import launch
import launch_ros.actions
import launch_testing
import launch_testing.actions
import launch_testing.asserts
import rclpy
from px4_msgs.msg import TrajectorySetpoint


def generate_test_description():
    controller_node = launch_ros.actions.Node(
        package="my_pkg",
        executable="controller_node",
        name="controller",
        output="screen",
    )

    return (
        launch.LaunchDescription([
            controller_node,
            # give the node 0.5 s to start before running tests
            launch.actions.TimerAction(
                period=0.5,
                actions=[launch_testing.actions.ReadyToTest()],
            ),
        ]),
        {"controller_node": controller_node},
    )


# Active tests -- run while the node is alive
class TestControllerActive(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        rclpy.init()

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        rclpy.shutdown()

    def setUp(self):
        # fresh node per test reduces cross-test interference
        self.node = rclpy.create_node("test_controller_listener")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.node.destroy_node()

    def test_publishes_trajectory_setpoint(self, proc_output):
        """Node must publish at least one TrajectorySetpoint within 10 s."""
        msgs = []
        sub = self.node.create_subscription(
            TrajectorySetpoint,
            "/fmu/in/trajectory_setpoint",
            lambda m: msgs.append(m),
            10,
        )
        try:
            end_time = time.time() + 10
            while time.time() < end_time:
                rclpy.spin_once(self.node, timeout_sec=1)
            assert len(msgs) > 0, "no TrajectorySetpoint received within 10 s"
        finally:
            self.node.destroy_subscription(sub)

    def test_logs_init(self, proc_output):
        """Node must log its startup message."""
        proc_output.assertWaitFor(
            "controller initialized",
            timeout=5,
            stream="stderr",
        )


# Post-shutdown tests -- run after all nodes exit
@launch_testing.post_shutdown_test()
class TestControllerShutdown(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_exit_codes(self, proc_info, controller_node):
        """All launched processes must exit cleanly."""
        launch_testing.asserts.assertExitCodes(
            proc_info, process=controller_node
        )


Domain isolation
By default, add_launch_test assigns domain ID 0 to every test, causing parallel tests to cross-talk. The ament_cmake_ros package ships a runner that picks a unique, free domain ID per test:
find_package(ament_cmake_ros REQUIRED)
find_package(launch_testing_ament_cmake REQUIRED)

function(add_ros_isolated_launch_test path)
  set(RUNNER "${ament_cmake_ros_DIR}/run_test_isolated.py")
  add_launch_test("${path}" RUNNER "${RUNNER}" ${ARGN})
endfunction()

add_ros_isolated_launch_test(test/test_integration.py)






Note



ROS_DOMAIN_ID must not be set in the environment when using the isolated runner — the coordinator selects a free ID automatically.




Full CMakeLists.txt snippet
if(BUILD_TESTING)
  # C++ unit tests
  find_package(ament_cmake_gtest REQUIRED)
  ament_add_gtest(test_math_utils test/test_math_utils.cpp)
  target_link_libraries(test_math_utils ${PROJECT_NAME})

  # Python unit tests
  find_package(ament_cmake_pytest REQUIRED)
  ament_add_pytest_test(test_utils test/test_math_utils.py)

  # Integration tests (isolated domain)
  find_package(ament_cmake_ros REQUIRED)
  find_package(launch_testing_ament_cmake REQUIRED)
  function(add_ros_isolated_launch_test path)
    set(RUNNER "${ament_cmake_ros_DIR}/run_test_isolated.py")
    add_launch_test("${path}" RUNNER "${RUNNER}" ${ARGN})
  endfunction()
  add_ros_isolated_launch_test(test/test_integration.py)
endif()

title: Testing ROS 2 Nodes
text:
Testing against SITL
For end-to-end tests that require a running flight stack, launch PX4 SITL and the DDS agent inside generate_test_description:
import launch
import launch.actions
import launch_ros.actions
import launch_testing
import launch_testing.actions


def generate_test_description():
    px4 = launch.actions.ExecuteProcess(
        cmd=["bash", "-c", "cd $PX4_ROOT && make px4_sitl gz_x500"],
        output="screen",
    )

    agent = launch_ros.actions.Node(
        package="micro_ros_agent",
        executable="micro_ros_agent",
        arguments=["udp4", "--port", "8888"],
        output="screen",
    )

    return (
        launch.LaunchDescription([
            px4,
            launch.actions.TimerAction(period=5.0, actions=[agent]),
            launch.actions.TimerAction(
                period=10.0,
                actions=[launch_testing.actions.ReadyToTest()],
            ),
        ]),
        {},
    )






Warning



SITL tests take 20–60 s each. Gate them behind a CMake option so CI can skip them on quick build checks:
option(TEST_SITL "Build SITL integration tests" OFF)
if(TEST_SITL)
  add_ros_isolated_launch_test(test/test_sitl.py)
endif()
Build with SITL tests enabled:
colcon build --cmake-args -DTEST_SITL=ON
colcon test  --packages-select my_pkg

title: Low-Level Offboard Control
text:
Low-level offboard control means bypassing PX4’s position/velocity controllers and sending commands directly to the inner loops. Three levels are available, selected at runtime via a ROS 2 parameter:
Reference implementation: SaxionMechatronics/px4_offboard_lowlevel.

text:
Frame conventions
PX4 uses NED / FRD (North-East-Down, Front-Right-Down). ROS and most controllers use ENU / FLU (East-North-Up, Front-Left-Up). All setpoints must be converted before publishing, and all odometry must be converted after reading.
See Frame Conventions for the full conversion reference including vector permutations, quaternion transforms, altitude sign, and yaw convention.

text:
Switching modes at runtime
The control mode can be changed without restarting the node:
ros2 param set /offboard_controller control_mode 2   # -> thrust + torque
ros2 param set /offboard_controller control_mode 3   # -> direct actuator
ros2 param set /offboard_controller control_mode 1   # -> attitude (default)
The OffboardControlMode heartbeat automatically switches its active field on the next publish cycle.

title: Control Allocation: Wrench to Motor Throttles
text:
Control allocation is the mapping from a desired wrench \([\tau_x,\, \tau_y,\, \tau_z,\, T]^\top\) to individual motor throttles \(\delta_i \in [0, 1]\). For an X-frame quadrotor it is a \(4 \times 4\) linear map followed by a square-root and an affine throttle scaling.
The implementation lives in motor_allocator.hpp inside uav_control.

title: Control Allocation: Wrench to Motor Throttles

Motor layout (x500 SITL, top view, NED)






Figure 1: x500 SITL X-frame motor layout with motor indices and spin directions.



Motor indices 0–3 map directly to ActuatorMotors.control[0..3]. Slots 4–11 must be NaN for a 4-motor vehicle.
crumbs: Control Allocation: Wrench to Motor Throttles

title: Control Allocation: Wrench to Motor Throttles
text:
Forward model
Each motor \(i\) spinning at \(\omega_i\) [rad/s] produces a thrust \(f_i = k_T \omega_i^2\) and a reaction torque \(m_i = k_m \omega_i^2\) where \(k_m = k_{M,\text{ratio}} \cdot k_T\).
The wrench assembled on the body is:
\[
\begin{pmatrix} \tau_x \\ \tau_y \\ \tau_z \\ T \end{pmatrix}
= \mathbf{A}\,\boldsymbol{\omega}^2,
\qquad
\mathbf{A} = \mathrm{diag}(k_T L,\; k_T L,\; k_m,\; k_T)\; \mathbf{B}
\]
where \(L\) is the arm length and \(\mathbf{B}\) encodes the geometry and spin directions:
\[
\mathbf{B} = \begin{pmatrix}
-k_s &  k_s &  k_s & -k_s \\
k_s & -k_s &  k_s & -k_s \\
    1 &    1 &   -1 &   -1 \\
    1 &    1 &    1 &    1
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad k_s = \sin 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
\]
Column order: FR(0), RL(1), FL(2), RR(3).

Row-by-row interpretation









Row
Wrench
Sign pattern
Reason




1
\(\tau_x\) (roll)
FR,RR negative; RL,FL positive
Right motors are on the \(+y\) side; spinning them faster rolls right (negative roll)


2
\(\tau_y\) (pitch)
RL,RR negative; FR,FL positive
Front motors are on the \(+x\) side


3
\(\tau_z\) (yaw)
FR,RL positive; FL,RR negative
CCW motors produce positive reaction torque on body


4
\(T\) (thrust)
all positive
All motors contribute thrust
crumbs: Control Allocation: Wrench to Motor Throttles

title: Control Allocation: Wrench to Motor Throttles
text:
Inverse: wrench -> throttles
The allocation inversion uses the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse:
\[
\boldsymbol{\omega}^2 = \mathbf{A}^+ \begin{pmatrix} \tau_x \\ \tau_y \\ \tau_z \\ T \end{pmatrix}
\]
Since \(\mathbf{A}\) is square and full rank for a standard quadrotor, \(\mathbf{A}^+
= \mathbf{A}^{-1}\).
Rotor speeds are then converted to throttles via:
\[
\omega_i = \sqrt{\max(0,\; \omega_i^2)}, \qquad
\delta_i = \mathrm{clip}\!\left(\frac{\omega_i - \omega_\min}{\omega_\max - \omega_\min},\; 0,\; 1\right)
\]
The \(\max(0,\cdot)\) before the square root prevents NaN from small negative values due to numerical noise.

title: Arming and Offboard Mode
text: Before a ROS 2 node can send setpoints to PX4, the vehicle must be armed and PX4 must be in offboard mode. Both transitions are triggered by publishing VehicleCommand messages. The sequence has strict ordering requirements and timing constraints.

title: Arming and Offboard Mode
text:
Required sequence
1. Start streaming OffboardControlMode heartbeat  (>=2 Hz, before switching)
2. Start streaming setpoints                       (same rate as control loop)
3. Send VehicleCommand: VEHICLE_CMD_DO_SET_MODE -> OFFBOARD
4. Send VehicleCommand: VEHICLE_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM -> ARM
Steps 1–2 must begin before step 3. PX4 rejects the offboard mode switch if it has not already seen a recent OffboardControlMode message. Keep both streams running continuously thereafter.

title: Arming and Offboard Mode
text:
Monitoring vehicle state
Subscribe to VehicleStatus to read the current arming and nav state:
#include <px4_msgs/msg/vehicle_status.hpp>

auto qos = rclcpp::QoS(10).best_effort();

status_sub_ = create_subscription<px4_msgs::msg::VehicleStatus>(
    "/fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1", qos,
    [this](const px4_msgs::msg::VehicleStatus::SharedPtr msg) {
        armed_       = (msg->arming_state ==
                        px4_msgs::msg::VehicleStatus::ARMING_STATE_ARMED);
        in_offboard_ = (msg->nav_state ==
                        px4_msgs::msg::VehicleStatus::NAVIGATION_STATE_OFFBOARD);
    });

text:
Troubleshooting

Vehicle never arms

Check pre-arm checks: ros2 topic echo /fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1 | grep arming.
In SITL, the EKF2 estimator must be healthy before arming. Wait ~5 s after SITL starts.
Ensure OffboardControlMode is being published before sending the arm command — PX4 refuses to arm for offboard if no heartbeat has arrived.



Offboard mode switch is accepted but vehicle falls
The OffboardControlMode was set with position = true but no TrajectorySetpoint is being published. The position controller has no target and commands zero thrust. Always publish a setpoint at the current position immediately after arming.


Vehicle disarms immediately after takeoff
The motor output stream (ActuatorMotors) stopped. PX4 exits offboard mode and auto-disarms. Check that your control timer is running without exceptions.

title: micro-XRCE-DDS Agent
text:
The micro-XRCE-DDS agent (also called the uXRCE-DDS agent or MicroXRCEAgent) is the bridge between PX4 and ROS 2. PX4 runs a micro-XRCE-DDS client internally; the agent runs on the companion computer (or SITL host) and forwards messages to the ROS 2 DDS middleware.
Without the agent, no /fmu/* topics appear and all ROS 2 subscribers receive nothing.

title: micro-XRCE-DDS Agent
text:
How it works
PX4 (SITL or hardware)           Companion / workstation
+------------------------+        +---------------------------+
| micro-XRCE-DDS client  | <----> | micro-XRCE-DDS agent      |
| (runs in PX4 firmware) |  UDP   | (MicroXRCEAgent binary)   |
+------------------------+        +-----------+---------------+
                                              |
                                       ROS 2 DDS (rmw)
                                              |
                                    +---------+---------+
                                    | /fmu/out/* topics |
                                    | /fmu/in/*  topics |
                                    +-------------------+
The agent converts between the XRCE wire protocol and native DDS. It is stateless — restart it freely without restarting PX4 or your ROS 2 nodes.

title: micro-XRCE-DDS Agent
text:
Installation

Option A – Snap (recommended for SITL on Ubuntu)
sudo snap install micro-xrce-dds-agent --edge
Run:
MicroXRCEAgent udp4 -p 8888


Option B – Build from source
git clone https://github.com/eProsima/Micro-XRCE-DDS-Agent.git
cd Micro-XRCE-DDS-Agent
mkdir build && cd build
cmake ..
make -j$(nproc)
sudo make install
Run:
MicroXRCEAgent udp4 -p 8888


Option C – pixi task (SITL-only)
Add the snap binary as a pixi task so it starts with the full SITL stack:
[tasks]
agent = "MicroXRCEAgent udp4 -p 8888"

px4-sitl = { cmd = "ros2 launch my_bringup px4_sitl.launch.py \
                    launch_px4:=true launch_agent:=true",
             depends-on = ["build"] }
The launch file is responsible for starting the agent subprocess — the agent task is kept separate for manual use.

title: micro-XRCE-DDS Agent
text:
Verifying the bridge
With PX4 SITL running and the agent started, open a new terminal inside the pixi environment and check that topics appear:
pixi shell
ros2 topic list | grep fmu
Expected output (subset):
/fmu/in/actuator_motors
/fmu/in/offboard_control_mode
/fmu/in/vehicle_attitude_setpoint
/fmu/in/vehicle_command
/fmu/in/vehicle_thrust_setpoint
/fmu/in/vehicle_torque_setpoint
/fmu/out/vehicle_angular_velocity
/fmu/out/vehicle_attitude
/fmu/out/vehicle_local_position
/fmu/out/vehicle_odometry
/fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1
If the list is empty, the agent is not connected. Check:

The agent process is running (ps aux | grep MicroXRCE).
Port 8888 is not blocked (ss -u -l -n | grep 8888).
PX4 printed INFO [uxrce_dds_client] synchronized with agent at startup.

Check publish rate on a key topic:
ros2 topic hz /fmu/out/vehicle_odometry
Expected: ~50 Hz. If rate is 0, the QoS profile is mismatched — see QoS Profiles.

title: micro-XRCE-DDS Agent
text:
Namespace isolation (multiple vehicles)
To run multiple SITL instances on the same machine, start each PX4 instance on a different port and run a separate agent for each:
# Vehicle 1
MicroXRCEAgent udp4 -p 8888 -n uav0

# Vehicle 2
MicroXRCEAgent udp4 -p 8889 -n uav1
The -n flag sets a ROS 2 namespace prefix. Topics appear as /uav0/fmu/out/... and /uav1/fmu/out/....

title: micro-XRCE-DDS Agent
text:
Troubleshooting

MicroXRCEAgent: command not found
The snap is not on PATH. Try /snap/bin/MicroXRCEAgent, or add /snap/bin to PATH in ~/.zshrc.


Agent connects but topics stop after a few seconds
PX4 SITL exited or crashed. The agent streams data only while the PX4 client is alive. Check the PX4 terminal for errors.


Topics appear but subscriber callbacks never fire
QoS mismatch. PX4 publishes with BEST_EFFORT reliability. See QoS Profiles.

title: C++ Node Package
text: A ROS 2 C++ package contains the compiled nodes that perform control, estimation, state machines, and any other compute-intensive logic. This page covers the minimal boilerplate to get a node building under colcon inside a pixi workspace.

title: C++ Node Package
text:
Directory layout
src/
+-- my_pkg/
    +-- include/
    |   +-- my_pkg/
    |       +-- controller.hpp
    |       +-- estimator.hpp
    +-- src/
    |   +-- controller.cpp
    |   +-- estimator.cpp
    |   +-- main.cpp
    +-- launch/
    |   +-- node.launch.py          # minimal single-node launch
    +-- CMakeLists.txt
    +-- package.xml
Headers live under include/<package_name>/ so they resolve as #include "my_pkg/controller.hpp" from any downstream package.

find_package(nav_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(px4_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(Eigen3 REQUIRED)

# --- shared library (enables composable-node registration) ---
add_library(${PROJECT_NAME} SHARED
  src/controller.cpp
  src/estimator.cpp
)

target_include_directories(${PROJECT_NAME} PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
  ${EIGEN3_INCLUDE_DIR}
)

target_compile_features(${PROJECT_NAME} PUBLIC cxx_std_17)

ament_target_dependencies(${PROJECT_NAME}
  rclcpp
  rclcpp_components
  std_msgs
  geometry_msgs
  nav_msgs
  px4_msgs
)

# --- register composable nodes ---
rclcpp_components_register_node(${PROJECT_NAME}
  PLUGIN "my_pkg::Controller"
  EXECUTABLE controller_node
)

rclcpp_components_register_node(${PROJECT_NAME}
  PLUGIN "my_pkg::Estimator"
  EXECUTABLE estimator_node
)

# --- install ---
install(TARGETS ${PROJECT_NAME}
  ARCHIVE DESTINATION lib
  LIBRARY DESTINATION lib
  RUNTIME DESTINATION bin
)

install(DIRECTORY include/ DESTINATION include)
install(DIRECTORY launch   DESTINATION share/${PROJECT_NAME})

ament_package()






Note



Building as a shared library and using rclcpp_components_register_node lets the bringup package load nodes in a ComponentContainer without spawning separate processes. The EXECUTABLE argument also produces a standalone binary for direct ros2 run use.

Project structure

+-- src/
|   +-- my_package/             # your ROS 2 packages
|   +-- px4_msgs/               # git submodule (PX4 message definitions)

title: Workspace Setup
text:
Workspace activation
Every time pixi launches a shell or runs a task it sources the scripts listed under [activation]. Use this to overlay the colcon install tree.
activate.sh (project root):
INSTALL_DIR="${PIXI_PROJECT_ROOT}/install"

if [ -f "${INSTALL_DIR}/setup.bash" ]; then
  source "${INSTALL_DIR}/setup.bash"
fi
PIXI_PROJECT_ROOT is set automatically to the directory containing pixi.toml. The if guard prevents errors on a clean checkout before the first build.

title: Workspace Setup
text:
PX4 message definitions (submodule)
px4_msgs must be built with colcon as a standard ROS 2 package. It is tracked as a git submodule so that the version is pinned to the exact PX4 firmware release you are flying against.

Adding the submodule
git submodule add -b release/1.16 \
    https://github.com/PX4/px4_msgs.git src/px4_msgs


Restoring on a fresh clone
git clone --recurse-submodules <repo-url>
# or, after a plain clone:
git submodule update --init --recursive


.gitmodules entry
[submodule "src/px4_msgs"]
    path   = src/px4_msgs
    url    = https://github.com/PX4/px4_msgs.git
    branch = release/1.16






Warning



Always pin px4_msgs to the same release branch as the PX4 firmware used for SITL (release/1.14, release/1.15, release/1.16, …). A mismatch produces silent serialization errors: topics publish but subscribers receive garbage.




Versioned topic names
From PX4 v1.14 onward, some topics are published under a versioned name to signal a breaking message-definition change. The most common case is VehicleStatus, which moved from:
/fmu/out/vehicle_status      # pre-v1.14
/fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1   # v1.14+
If your subscriber listens on the wrong topic name it receives no data at all — the subscription simply never fires. Auto-arming logic that waits for arming_state == ARMING_STATE_ARMED blocks forever, and the vehicle never arms.
The fix is to subscribe to the versioned topic:
// px4_interface.cpp / px4_manager_node.cpp
status_sub_ = node_->create_subscription<px4_msgs::msg::VehicleStatus>(
    "/fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1", qos, callback);
Check which topics are actually being published by the running firmware:
ros2 topic list | grep vehicle_status
Use whichever name appears — it tells you exactly what the firmware is advertising.


Diagnosing version mismatches
If the topic name is correct but arming still fails, the submodule and firmware are on different releases (fields added/removed between releases cause silent deserialization errors). Check alignment:
# commit that your workspace px4_msgs is pinned to
git -C src/px4_msgs rev-parse HEAD

# PX4 version string printed at SITL startup, e.g. "PX4 v1.15.2"
# must correspond to the same release branch
To fix, update the submodule to the branch matching your firmware:
cd src/px4_msgs
git fetch
git checkout release/1.16   # match PX4 firmware version
cd ../..
colcon build --symlink-install
git add src/px4_msgs
git commit -m "chore: pin px4_msgs to release/1.16"

title: Workspace Setup
text:
Build tasks
Define all build and launch operations as pixi tasks. Every task runs inside the activated environment, so ros2, colcon, cmake, and nvcc are all on PATH.
[tasks]
# Build all packages with symlink install and compile commands export
build = "colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=1"

# Remove all colcon output
clean = "rm -rf build install log"

# Run all tests with live console output
test = "colcon test --event-handlers console_direct+"

# Launch control nodes only (PX4 running externally)
launch = { cmd = "ros2 launch my_bringup sitl.launch.py",
           depends-on = ["build"] }

# Full SITL stack: PX4 + micro-XRCE-DDS agent + control nodes
px4-sitl = { cmd = "ros2 launch my_bringup px4_sitl.launch.py \
                     launch_px4:=true launch_agent:=true record_bag:=false",
             depends-on = ["build"] }

# Canned trajectories
hover = { cmd = "ros2 launch my_bringup px4_sitl.launch.py \
                 launch_px4:=true launch_agent:=true \
                 trajectory_type:=hover z:=2.0 duration:=90.0",
          depends-on = ["build"] }

lemniscate = { cmd = "ros2 launch my_bringup px4_sitl.launch.py \
                      launch_px4:=true launch_agent:=true \
                      trajectory_type:=lemniscate A:=3.0 omega:=0.2 z:=2.0",
               depends-on = ["build"] }

circular = { cmd = "ros2 launch my_bringup px4_sitl.launch.py \
                    launch_px4:=true launch_agent:=true \
                    trajectory_type:=circular A:=3.0 omega:=0.2 z:=2.0",
             depends-on = ["build"] }
Run any task with:
pixi run build
pixi run px4-sitl
pixi run hover
The depends-on field guarantees the workspace is rebuilt before launching.

The colcon install overlay is stale. Run pixi run build.


ros2: command not found inside pixi shell
The activation script did not run. Verify:

activate.sh exists at the project root.

You entered the environment with pixi shell or pixi run <task>.



CUDA compiler (nvcc) not found
Only needed if your workspace has GPU-accelerated nodes.

Run pixi install to fetch it.
Inside pixi shell, which nvcc should resolve to .pixi/envs/default/bin/nvcc.

title: PX4 SITL Setup
text: This page covers how to build PX4 firmware, launch the Gazebo SITL simulator, and wire it into the pixi workspace for use with the ROS 2 integration.

title: PX4 SITL Setup
text:
Prerequisites
PX4 SITL requires a native Ubuntu build environment. The PX4 source tree is not managed inside the ROS 2 workspace — it lives separately and is built with its own toolchain.
# Install PX4 build dependencies (run once)
git clone https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot.git --recursive
cd PX4-Autopilot
bash ./Tools/setup/ubuntu.sh






Note



ubuntu.sh installs system packages including gcc-arm-none-eabi, ninja, and Python dependencies. It also installs gz-harmonic (Gazebo) for SITL. Re-run it if a new PX4 checkout changes the required dependencies.

title: PX4 SITL Setup
text:
Building and launching
cd PX4-Autopilot
make px4_sitl gz_x500
This compiles the SITL binary and launches both PX4 and the Gazebo GUI. The first build takes ~5 minutes; subsequent builds are incremental.
On launch, PX4 prints its version string (PX4 v1.16.x) and drops into the NuttShell:
nsh>
Confirm the build binary exists:
ls build/px4_sitl_default/bin/px4

title: PX4 SITL Setup
text:
Standalone mode
In standalone mode PX4 and Gazebo run in separate terminals. This is useful for attaching to an already-running Gazebo instance, or for running them on different machines.
Terminal 1 — start Gazebo:
# Download the simulation-gazebo launcher script (once)
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PX4/PX4-gazebo-models/main/simulation-gazebo
python3 simulation-gazebo
simulation-gazebo downloads models and worlds to ~/.simulation-gazebo on first run and re-uses them on subsequent runs.
Terminal 2 — start PX4:
cd PX4-Autopilot
PX4_GZ_STANDALONE=1 make px4_sitl gz_x500
PX4 will print WARN [gz bridge] Service call timed out until Gazebo starts — this is normal. Once Gazebo is up, PX4 connects automatically.

title: PX4 SITL Setup
PX4 SITL Setup
text:
Confirming SITL is running
Check EKF and commander state from the NuttShell:
nsh> ekf2 status
nsh> commander status
In a separate terminal, confirm DDS topics appear after starting the micro-XRCE-DDS agent (see DDS Agent Setup):
ros2 topic list | grep fmu

title: PX4 SITL Setup
text:
Troubleshooting

ninja: error: unknown target 'gz_x500'
The build tree is stale. Run make distclean then retry:
make distclean
make px4_sitl gz_x500


make px4_sitl gz_x500 fails with missing submodules
The PX4 repo was cloned without --recursive:
git submodule update --init --recursive


Gazebo window does not open
The display is not forwarded or the GPU driver lacks OpenGL 3.3 support. Either set HEADLESS=1, or try the OGRE 1 renderer:
PX4_GZ_SIM_RENDER_ENGINE=ogre make px4_sitl gz_x500


PX4 exits immediately after launch
Lockstep is waiting for a Gazebo clock. Ensure Gazebo is running — the gz_x500 target launches both. In standalone mode, start Gazebo before PX4.


EKF2 ERROR at startup
Normal for the first ~5 s while sensors initialise. If it persists, check that gz-harmonic is installed and the Gazebo sensors plugin loaded without errors.

title: Bringup Package
text:
A bringup package follows the nav2 convention: it contains only launch files, YAML parameter files, and static assets (RViz configs, maps). It has no compiled code of its own — it just wires together the node packages and configures them for a specific deployment.
Keeping bringup separate from node code means you can reconfigure a full system without recompiling anything.

title: Bringup Package
text:
Directory layout
src/
+-- my_bringup/
    +-- launch/
    |   +-- bringup.launch.py      # top-level entry point
    |   +-- nodes.launch.py        # node composition sub-launch
    |   +-- sim.launch.py          # simulation-specific overrides
    +-- params/
    |   +-- controller.yaml
    |   +-- estimator.yaml
    +-- rviz/
    |   +-- default.rviz
    +-- CMakeLists.txt
    +-- package.xml

title: Bringup Package
Bringup Package
text:
CMakeLists.txt
The CMakeLists.txt only installs the non-compiled assets.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
project(my_bringup)

find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)

install(DIRECTORY launch params rviz
  DESTINATION share/${PROJECT_NAME}
)

ament_package()

title: Bringup Package
text:
Top-level launch — launch/bringup.launch.py
The top-level file declares user-facing arguments and delegates to sub-launches. Mirrors the nav2 bringup_launch.py pattern.
import os
from ament_index_python.packages import get_package_share_directory
from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch.actions import (
    DeclareLaunchArgument,
    GroupAction,
    IncludeLaunchDescription,
    OpaqueFunction,
)
from launch.conditions import IfCondition
from launch.launch_description_sources import PythonLaunchDescriptionSource
from launch.substitutions import LaunchConfiguration, PathJoinSubstitution
from launch_ros.substitutions import FindPackageShare


def generate_launch_description():
    bringup_dir = get_package_share_directory("my_bringup")

    # --- declare arguments ---
    use_sim_time_arg = DeclareLaunchArgument(
        "use_sim_time",
        default_value="true",
        description="Use simulation (Gazebo) clock",
    )
    namespace_arg = DeclareLaunchArgument(
        "namespace",
        default_value="",
        description="Top-level namespace",
    )
    params_file_arg = DeclareLaunchArgument(
        "params_file",
        default_value=os.path.join(bringup_dir, "params", "controller.yaml"),
        description="Path to the controller parameter file",
    )
    use_rviz_arg = DeclareLaunchArgument(
        "use_rviz",
        default_value="true",
        description="Launch RViz",
    )

    # --- sub-launches ---
    nodes_launch = IncludeLaunchDescription(
        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(
            os.path.join(bringup_dir, "launch", "nodes.launch.py")
        ),
        launch_arguments={
            "use_sim_time": LaunchConfiguration("use_sim_time"),
            "namespace":    LaunchConfiguration("namespace"),
            "params_file":  LaunchConfiguration("params_file"),
        }.items(),
    )

    rviz_node = IncludeLaunchDescription(
        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(
            os.path.join(bringup_dir, "launch", "rviz.launch.py")
        ),
        condition=IfCondition(LaunchConfiguration("use_rviz")),
    )

    return LaunchDescription([
        use_sim_time_arg,
        namespace_arg,
        params_file_arg,
        use_rviz_arg,
        nodes_launch,
        rviz_node,
    ])

title: Bringup Package
text:
Composable nodes — launch/nodes.launch.py
Loading nodes into a shared ComponentContainer avoids inter-process message serialization and is the nav2 standard for production deployments.
import os
from ament_index_python.packages import get_package_share_directory
from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch.actions import DeclareLaunchArgument, GroupAction
from launch.substitutions import LaunchConfiguration
from launch_ros.actions import ComposableNodeContainer, Node
from launch_ros.descriptions import ComposableNode


def generate_launch_description():
    params_file = LaunchConfiguration("params_file")
    use_sim_time = LaunchConfiguration("use_sim_time")
    namespace    = LaunchConfiguration("namespace")

    container = ComposableNodeContainer(
        name="my_container",
        namespace=namespace,
        package="rclcpp_components",
        executable="component_container",
        composable_node_descriptions=[
            ComposableNode(
                package="my_pkg",
                plugin="my_pkg::Controller",
                name="controller",
                parameters=[params_file, {"use_sim_time": use_sim_time}],
                remappings=[
                    ("/fmu/out/vehicle_odometry", "/fmu/out/vehicle_odometry"),
                ],
            ),
            ComposableNode(
                package="my_pkg",
                plugin="my_pkg::Estimator",
                name="estimator",
                parameters=[params_file, {"use_sim_time": use_sim_time}],
            ),
        ],
        output="screen",
    )

    return LaunchDescription([
        DeclareLaunchArgument("params_file"),
        DeclareLaunchArgument("use_sim_time", default_value="true"),
        DeclareLaunchArgument("namespace",    default_value=""),
        container,
    ])






Note



ComposableNode requires that the node package registers its plugin with rclcpp_components_register_node in CMakeLists.txt — see the C++ Node Package page.

title: Bringup Package
text:
YAML parameter file — params/controller.yaml
Parameter files follow the standard ROS 2 format: <node_name> -> ros__parameters -> key-value pairs. Relative node names (no leading /) apply regardless of namespace.
controller:
  ros__parameters:
    control_rate_hz: 50.0
    max_velocity_mps: 5.0
    max_acceleration_mpss: 3.0

estimator:
  ros__parameters:
    use_sim_time: true
    process_noise_std: 0.01
    measurement_noise_std: 0.05






Tip



Separate controller.yaml and estimator.yaml files work fine; just pass both in the parameters list of ComposableNode: parameters=[controller_params, estimator_params, {"use_sim_time": use_sim_time}]

title: Bringup Package
section: Passing launch arguments from the CLI
text:
Passing launch arguments from the CLI
# default (sim, with RViz)
ros2 launch my_bringup bringup.launch.py

# hardware run without RViz, custom params
ros2 launch my_bringup bringup.launch.py \
  use_sim_time:=false \
  use_rviz:=false \
  params_file:=/path/to/hw_params.yaml
Via pixi (add a task in pixi.toml):
[tasks]
bringup     = "ros2 launch my_bringup bringup.launch.py"
bringup-hw  = "ros2 launch my_bringup bringup.launch.py use_sim_time:=false use_rviz:=false"
pixi run bringup
pixi run bringup-hw

title: Bringup Package
text:
Building
The bringup package has nothing to compile; colcon still needs to process it to install the share files:
pixi run build
Because the assets are installed (not symlinked by default under --merge-install), you must rebuild after editing YAML files or launch scripts. Use --symlink-install to skip this:
colcon build --symlink-install --packages-select my_bringup

title: Bringup Package
text:
Simulation override — launch/sim.launch.py
A separate simulation sub-launch can start Gazebo and the DDS agent before including the main bringup:
from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch.actions import IncludeLaunchDescription
from launch.launch_description_sources import PythonLaunchDescriptionSource
from ament_index_python.packages import get_package_share_directory
import os


def generate_launch_description():
    bringup_dir = get_package_share_directory("my_bringup")

    # start Gazebo + PX4 SITL (adapt to your sim launch)
    sitl_launch = IncludeLaunchDescription(
        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(
            os.path.join(
                get_package_share_directory("px4_sitl_launch"),
                "launch", "gazebo.launch.py",
            )
        )
    )

    system_launch = IncludeLaunchDescription(
        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(
            os.path.join(bringup_dir, "launch", "bringup.launch.py")
        ),
        launch_arguments={"use_sim_time": "true"}.items(),
    )

    return LaunchDescription([sitl_launch, system_launch])

title: ROS 2 Package Structure
text: This page describes the minimal layout and boilerplate for a ROS 2 C++ package that builds correctly under colcon inside the pixi workspace.

title: ROS 2 Package Structure
text:
Directory layout
src/
+-- my_package/
    +-- include/
    |   +-- my_package/
    |       +-- my_node.hpp
    +-- src/
    |   +-- my_node.cpp
    |   +-- main.cpp
    +-- launch/
    |   +-- my_node.launch.py
    +-- CMakeLists.txt
    +-- package.xml
Headers live under include/<package_name>/ so they are importable as #include "my_package/my_node.hpp" from any package that depends on this one.

title: ROS 2 Package Structure
ROS 2 Package Structure
text:
CMakeLists.txt
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
project(my_package)

# --- compiler settings ---
if(CMAKE_COMPILER_IS_GNUCXX OR CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "Clang")
  add_compile_options(-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic)
endif()

# --- find dependencies ---
find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
find_package(rclcpp REQUIRED)
find_package(std_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(geometry_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(px4_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(Eigen3 REQUIRED)

# --- build target ---
add_executable(my_node
  src/my_node.cpp
  src/main.cpp
)

target_include_directories(my_node PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
  ${EIGEN3_INCLUDE_DIR}
)

target_compile_features(my_node PUBLIC cxx_std_17)

ament_target_dependencies(my_node
  rclcpp
  std_msgs
  geometry_msgs
  px4_msgs
)

# --- install ---
install(TARGETS my_node DESTINATION lib/${PROJECT_NAME})
install(DIRECTORY launch DESTINATION share/${PROJECT_NAME})

ament_package()






Note



ament_target_dependencies handles both include paths and link libraries for ament packages. Only use target_link_libraries for non-ament deps (Eigen, yaml-cpp, etc.) that expose CMake targets directly.

title: ROS 2 Package Structure
ROS 2 Package Structure
text:
Launch file
launch/my_node.launch.py:
from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch_ros.actions import Node


def generate_launch_description():
    return LaunchDescription([
        Node(
            package="my_package",
            executable="my_node",
            name="my_node",
            output="screen",
            parameters=[],
        )
    ])
Launch with:
ros2 launch my_package my_node.launch.py
Or via pixi:
pixi run launch   # if you defined a 'launch' task in pixi.toml

title: ROS 2 Package Structure
text:
Building and running
# Build the workspace (all packages under src/)
pixi run build

# Run the node directly
pixi run -- ros2 run my_package my_node

# Or via launch file
pixi run -- ros2 launch my_package my_node.launch.py
After editing source files, re-run pixi run build. With --symlink-install (default in the build task), Python and resource files are symlinked so they update without a rebuild — C++ sources still require a rebuild.

title: ROS 2 Package Structure
text:
Adding a new package

Create the directory under src/:
mkdir -p src/my_new_package/{include/my_new_package,src,launch}
Write package.xml and CMakeLists.txt as shown above.
Run pixi run build — colcon discovers the new package automatically.

No registration in pixi.toml is needed. colcon scans src/ recursively for package.xml files.

title: QoS Profiles for PX4 Topics
text: ROS 2 Quality of Service (QoS) settings must match between publisher and subscriber. PX4 publishes all /fmu/out/* topics with BEST_EFFORT reliability. If your subscriber uses the default RELIABLE profile, ROS 2 silently drops the connection — the subscription is created with no error, but the callback never fires.

title: QoS Profiles for PX4 Topics
text:
Why QoS mismatches are silent
ROS 2 DDS does not error on a QoS incompatibility. The subscription is registered, the topic appears in ros2 topic list, but the middleware determines the publisher and subscriber are incompatible and simply sends no data. ros2 topic hz reports 0 Hz.

title: QoS Profiles for PX4 Topics
text:
PX4 publisher profile
All PX4 /fmu/out/* topics use:



Setting
Value




Reliability
BEST_EFFORT


Durability
VOLATILE


History
KEEP_LAST(10)



BEST_EFFORT means packets may be dropped under load — acceptable for high-rate sensor streams where stale data is worse than missing data. VOLATILE means the publisher does not persist messages for late-joining subscribers.

title: QoS Profiles for PX4 Topics
QoS Profiles for PX4 Topics
QoS Profiles for PX4 Topics
QoS Profiles for PX4 Topics
text:
Diagnosing a mismatch
# Check publisher QoS
ros2 topic info /fmu/out/vehicle_odometry --verbose

# Expected:
# Publisher count: 1
#   QoS profile:
#     Reliability: BEST_EFFORT
#     Durability: VOLATILE
If your subscriber shows Reliability: RELIABLE while the publisher shows BEST_EFFORT, the middleware will log an incompatibility warning at the DEBUG level. Enable it:
export RCUTILS_LOGGING_SEVERITY=DEBUG
ros2 run my_package my_node
# look for: "NEW_QOS_POLICY_REQUEST_INCOMPATIBLE_QOS"

title: QoS Profiles for PX4 Topics
text:
Python subscribers
The same rule applies to rclpy:
from rclpy.qos import QoSProfile, ReliabilityPolicy, DurabilityPolicy

px4_qos = QoSProfile(
    reliability=ReliabilityPolicy.BEST_EFFORT,
    durability=DurabilityPolicy.VOLATILE,
    depth=10,
)

self.sub = self.create_subscription(
    VehicleOdometry,
    "/fmu/out/vehicle_odometry",
    self.callback,
    px4_qos,
)

Summary



Topic direction

VOLATILE



Use .best_effort() on every QoS object that touches a PX4 topic. There are no exceptions.

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text: This guide covers how to configure basedpyright for a ROS 2 workspace managed with pixi. basedpyright is a stricter fork of pyright with better defaults and improved error messages.

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
Why basedpyright
Standard pyright works fine for general Python, but ROS 2 introduces friction:

rclpy, px4_msgs, and most ROS packages ship no type stubs.
Generated message classes have loose constructors that trigger false-positive argument-type errors.
The install tree lives in install/ (a colcon artifact), not in the standard site-packages location.

basedpyright provides more granular per-rule configuration so you can silence ROS-specific false positives while still catching real errors in your own code.

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
Installation

Inside the pixi environment (recommended)
Add basedpyright to a dev feature so it is not bundled into production builds:
# pixi.toml
[feature.dev.pypi-dependencies]
basedpyright = "*"

[environments]
dev = { features = ["dev"], solve-group = "default" }
Install and run:
pixi install -e dev
pixi run -e dev basedpyright src/


Global install (for the LSP / editor)
# via pip
pip install basedpyright

# via npm (also installs the language server)
npm install -g basedpyright
The VSCode extension is basedpyright (detachhead.basedpyright). Do not mix an npm install with the VSCode extension – let the extension manage its own binary.

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
pyrightconfig.json
Place pyrightconfig.json at the workspace root (same directory as pixi.toml).
{
  "typeCheckingMode": "basic",
  "pythonVersion": "3.11",
  "pythonPlatform": "Linux",

  "include": ["src"],
  "exclude": [
    "**/node_modules",
    "**/__pycache__",
    "**/.*",
    "build",
    "install",
    "log"
  ],

  "reportMissingImports": true,
  "reportMissingTypeStubs": false,

  "reportUnusedImport": true,
  "reportUnusedVariable": true,

  "reportGeneralTypeIssues": true,
  "reportOptionalMemberAccess": true,
  "reportOptionalSubscript": true,
  "reportOptionalOperand": true,
  "reportOptionalIterable": true,
  "reportOptionalContextManager": true,
  "reportOptionalCallOperand": true,

  "reportArgumentType": false
}

Settings explained








Setting
Value
Reason




typeCheckingMode
"basic"
Avoids false positives from untyped ROS packages. Upgrade to "standard" once stubs improve.


pythonVersion
"3.11"
Must match the Python version in pixi.toml.


include
["src"]
Only analyse your packages; ignore colcon build artefacts.


exclude
build, install, log
Colcon output contains generated C-extension stubs that confuse the checker.


reportMissingTypeStubs
false
rclpy, px4_msgs, and most ROS packages have no .pyi stubs.


reportArgumentType
false
Generated message classes have loose __init__ signatures that produce spurious errors.

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
section: Pointing basedpyright at the pixi environment
text:
Pointing basedpyright at the pixi environment
basedpyright must resolve imports from the pixi environment, not system Python.

Option A – venvPath (recommended)
{
  "venvPath": ".",
  "venv": ".pixi/envs/default"
}
This tells basedpyright to look for the virtual environment at .pixi/envs/default relative to the project root.


Option B – pythonPath
{
  "pythonPath": ".pixi/envs/default/bin/python"
}
Use this if venvPath does not correctly resolve stubs.






Tip



Verify interpreter resolution:
basedpyright --outputjson src/ 2>&1 | python -m json.tool | grep pythonPath

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
ROS 2-specific notes

rclpy stubs
rclpy has partial stubs on PyPI. They are often outdated but reduce reportMissingTypeStubs noise:
[feature.dev.pypi-dependencies]
rclpy-stubs = "*"
Alternatively, generate stubs from the installed package:
# inside pixi shell
stubgen -p rclpy -o typestubs/
Then register the stub path in pyrightconfig.json:
{
  "stubPath": "typestubs"
}


px4_msgs
px4_msgs is a C extension built by colcon. After building, point basedpyright to its install location:
{
  "extraPaths": [
    "install/px4_msgs/lib/python3.11/site-packages"
  ]
}
If you used venvPath above and the pixi activation already sourced install/setup.bash, this may not be necessary.


Launch files
ROS 2 launch files (.launch.py) use dynamic LaunchArgument substitutions that cannot be statically analysed. Suppress errors per-file:
# pyright: reportGeneralTypeIssues=false

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
VSCode integration
Add to .vscode/settings.json:
{
  "python.defaultInterpreterPath":
      "${workspaceFolder}/.pixi/envs/default/bin/python",

  "basedpyright.pythonPath":
      "${workspaceFolder}/.pixi/envs/default/bin/python",

  "basedpyright.disableOrganizeImports": false
}
python.defaultInterpreterPath ensures the VSCode Python extension, IntelliSense, and basedpyright all share the same pixi interpreter.

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
Running from the CLI
# Check all packages under src/
pixi run -e dev basedpyright src/

# Check a single package
pixi run -e dev basedpyright src/my_package/

# JSON output for CI
pixi run -e dev basedpyright --outputjson src/ > typecheck.json

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
Incrementally tightening type checking
Start at "basic" to suppress ROS-stub noise. Tighten per-package as you add type annotations or as upstream stubs improve.
basic  ->  standard  ->  strict  ->  all
To apply stricter checking to a specific file, add a comment at the top:
# pyright: standard
To apply it to an entire subtree, add a nested pyrightconfig.json in that subdirectory with only the overridden key:
{
  "typeCheckingMode": "standard"
}
The root pyrightconfig.json still governs everything else.

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text: This guide covers the .clangd configuration used across uav_control and related ROS 2 C++ packages. The setup gives accurate clangd completions and clang-tidy diagnostics inside a colcon workspace without false positives from GPU or ROS-specific compiler flags.

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
How clangd finds headers
clangd reads compile_commands.json to know which flags were used to build each translation unit. colcon generates this file at the workspace root when you pass --cmake-args -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON:
colcon build --cmake-args -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON
The .clangd file then tells clangd where to look:
CompileFlags:
    CompilationDatabase: "."
"." resolves to the directory containing .clangd, which should be the workspace root (the directory that contains src/, build/, install/).

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
Base configuration
CompileFlags:
    CompilationDatabase: "."
    Add: ["-std=c++17", "-Wno-unknown-argument"]
    Remove:
        [
            "--generate-code=*",
            "--options-file",
            "--options-file=*",
            "-rdc=*",
            "-forward-unknown-to-host-compiler",
            "-Xcompiler=*",
            "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
        ]
The Remove list strips NVCC-specific flags that clang does not understand. Without this, clangd crashes or emits spurious errors on any package that links against CUDA.
-Wno-unknown-argument suppresses the resulting unknown-flag warnings for any flags not caught by the Remove list.

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
clang-tidy checks
The project runs the full clang-tidy suite (Add: ["*"]) with a focused suppress list. The suppressed checks fall into two categories:
Style preferences — rules that conflict with the project’s conventions:







Check
Reason suppressed




google-build-*, google-readability-*
Google style not used


modernize-use-trailing-return-type
Trailing return types add noise for simple functions


modernize-use-nodiscard
Overly noisy for internal helpers


readability-identifier-length
Short names (e.g. dt, u) are idiomatic in control code


readability-magic-numbers, cppcoreguidelines-avoid-magic-numbers
Physical constants and gains are fine inline


readability-function-cognitive-complexity
MPPI kernels are inherently long



False positives in ROS 2 / robotics code:







Check
Reason suppressed




cppcoreguidelines-avoid-non-const-global-variables
ROS node handles and parameter servers are globals by convention


cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-vararg
Some ROS logging macros use varargs


cppcoreguidelines-pro-bounds-array-to-pointer-decay
Common in Eigen / low-level math


cppcoreguidelines-special-member-functions, hicpp-special-member-functions
Rule-of-five is not required for RAII wrappers with shared_ptr


misc-non-private-member-variables-in-classes, cppcoreguidelines-non-private-member-variables-in-classes
Parameter structs use public fields intentionally


cppcoreguidelines-prefer-member-initializer
Conflicts with complex constructor delegation patterns


misc-include-cleaner
Generates excessive noise from transitively included ROS headers



Vendor-specific suites (llvmlibc-*, fuchsia-*, altera-*) are suppressed wholesale as they target entirely different platforms.

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
CUDA file handling
.cu files need special treatment because compile_commands.json records the NVCC invocation, not a clang-compatible command. A conditional block remaps them to clang with CUDA-host-only parsing:
---
If:
    PathMatch: ".*\\.cu$"
CompileFlags:
    Compiler: clang++
    Add:
        [
            "-xcuda",
            "--cuda-host-only",
            "--cuda-path=/usr/local/cuda",
            "--cuda-gpu-arch=sm_75",
            "-Wno-unknown-cuda-version",
            "-ferror-limit=0",
        ]
    Remove:
        [
            "/usr/local/cuda-*/bin/nvcc",
            "--generate-code=*",
            "--options-file",
            "--options-file=*",
            "-rdc=*",
            "-forward-unknown-to-host-compiler",
            "-Xcompiler=*",
            "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
            "-x", "cu", "cuda",
        ]
Diagnostics:
    Suppress:
        - "cuda_ovl_target"
        - "redefinition"
        - "constexpr_redecl_mismatch"
        - "variadic_device_fn"
        - "attributes_not_allowed"
        - "undeclared_var_use"
--cuda-host-only tells clang to only parse host code, which avoids the need for a full CUDA device compiler toolchain. The Suppress list silences redefinition errors that arise from CUDA’s dual-compilation model.
Adjust --cuda-gpu-arch to match your GPU (e.g. sm_86 for Ampere, sm_89 for Ada Lovelace).

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
Placement
Put .clangd at the workspace root (the directory that contains src/), not inside individual packages. clangd searches upward from the open file to find the nearest .clangd, so a single workspace-root file covers all packages.
my_ws/
  .clangd            <-- here
  compile_commands.json
  src/
    uav_control/
    px4_msgs/

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
Troubleshooting

clangd cannot find compile_commands.json
Run a full build with compile commands export enabled:
colcon build --cmake-args -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON
Then confirm the file exists at the workspace root:
ls compile_commands.json


False-positive #include errors after adding a new package
colcon build must be re-run so the new package’s headers appear in compile_commands.json. clangd will re-index automatically once the file is updated.


clangd crashes on .cu files
Confirm clang++ is on PATH inside the pixi environment:
pixi run which clang++
If missing, add clangxx (or clang) to [dependencies] in pixi.toml.
